ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a human reviewer: route-deviation refund cannot be auto-computed while the SAFE-1 abuse finding stands. Route the abuse finding against the driver to Ryde's conduct/account team for review, keep the metered-fare overcharge claim open for manual fare review, and note that the rider described feeling unsafe.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the driver's chat reply "Shut up and let me drive." at 09:05:45, sent in answer to the rider's (civil) query "Why are we going this way? This is not the route on the app.", is hostile/abusive language aimed at the other party. Ryde's code of conduct bars abuse of any kind, so this is at least a suspected SAFE-1 violation and the case must go to a human rather than receive an automatic refund. The rider's "felt unsafe" is read as consequent to that exchange; there is no collision, injury or dangerous-driving allegation (SAFE-2 not engaged).

Route: requested pick-up at Marina Bay Sands, drop-off Tampines Mall, quoted route 15.88 km / 21.4 min. Trace (30 s thinning): the driver followed the quoted corridor up the northbound ECP/KPE stretch until the vicinity of 1.3233/103.8946 (~08:59:30), then doubled back on the same stretch (~09:00:00-09:02:00) and wandered between 09:02:00 and 09:10:00 before resuming eastward, reaching Tampines Mall at 09:21:00. Sampled GPS ground distance is ~27.5 km (dense 5 s grid would be slightly longer), against the 15.88 km quotation — a materially longer actual path, so the RD-1 picture is a large detour rather than matched noise. The fare record itself shows the meter charging 21.43 km at $1.41/km = $30.22, i.e. ~5.55 km beyond the quote; at the metered distance rate that is ~$7.83, so any RD-2 refund would be substantial, not nominal.

Exemptions do not resolve it: the driver's statement ("I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted") is uncorroborated — no reroute log or navigation record — and no `traffic-incident-*` fact exists (incidents list empty). The KPE speed band in the record is band 4 (not band 1/2), and the PIE band-5 link's geometry matches the route the driver did partly take, not any part of the optimal route he left, so RD-4(a)/(b) give no exemption to any off-route portion. There is no rider message consenting to any route change before the deviation began, so RD-5 is not satisfied.

Because the classification of the segments (and therefore the refund amount and any account flag under RD-6) cannot be settled by an automatic ruling while the abuse finding stands, the whole case is escalated; the factual summary above is the input for the human reviewer. Confidence 0.62 reflects the clear abuse finding but an approximate segment accounting derived from a thinned trace.
ruling.escalation_reason: SAFE-1 suspected: abuse aimed at the rider in the in-app chat ("Shut up and let me drive."). Per policy no automatic ruling is issued on a safety-flagged case; the route-deviation/overcharge computation (materially longer metered path: 21.43 km charged vs 15.88 km quoted, ~$7.83 meter excess at $1.41/km, no RD-4/RD-5 exemption) is supplied for the human reviewer to finalise together with the conduct finding.

segment_findings.reason: The backward turn and local wandering (approx. 08:59:00-09:10:00) deviate from the quoted optimal route and add materially to the metered distance. RD-1: no reasonable cause shown — the driver's uncorroborated 'GPS rerouted' claim is not a record; RD-4(a) fails (no traffic-incident fact), RD-4(b) fails (KPE band 4, not 1/2; the PIE band-5 link matches the route actually driven, not the optimal route); RD-5 fails (no rider consent before the deviation). Given the safety escalation the exact segment boundaries and extra_km are for the human reviewer to finalise.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's account that the GPS rerouted him is uncorroborated: no navigation/reroute record, no traffic incident on the optimal route, and the only speed-band facts concern the route actually driven or show band 4. System records (GPS trace, fare) override statements.

The rider's 'I was overcharged' is directionally supported (metered 21.43 km vs 15.88 km quoted; ~$7.83 of meter excess at $1.41/km), but the exact RD-2 amount cannot be finalised automatically from a 30 s thinned trace, and the case is escalated for the safety finding before any refund executes.

safety_basis: Driver chat at 09:05:45 in reply to the rider's route question: "Shut up and let me drive." — hostile/abusive language aimed at the rider (SAFE-1, Ryde code of conduct barring abuse of any kind).
Rider complaint: "...when I asked he told me to shut up. I was overcharged and felt unsafe."
